archetype: A WU forced-draw punisher. Ten symmetric table-draw engines feed six asymmetric hand-size punishers; eight counterspells buy the turns; two checker-passed kills sit behind it (Approach of the Second Sun in stack 002, the Aetherflux Reservoir storm in stack 006). deck-audit reads `control` from strategic_frame.json and applies the control overrides. The frame agrees with the deck; the overrides do not — they ask 5-7 wipes and 37-39 lands of a deck that wins off a life ledger and an upkeep clock. card_roles.json classifies 85.9% of the 99 and the twelve it misses include Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke and Propaganda — which are the deck's identity, so every role-derived count here is a floor.
verdict: The engine turns over and the deck never runs out of cards: the table-draw half is drawn in 85.2% of goldfish games, the punisher half in 67.2%, both in 56.7%, on a 0.866 turn-three land-drop rate and six checker-passed stacks. What binds is white mana at the point of deployment — 18 white sources against a target of 36, and a measured 0.515 probability of two white sources on curve against blue's 0.804, in a deck whose commander costs {2}{W}{W}. Behind that sits a ceiling the mana fix does not touch: the verified Reservoir kill assembles in 0.7% of goldfish games, and in the deck's one 20-game pod run it dealt a median 0 combat damage and no elimination in the run was attributed to it. Buy the colour first; the kill is a separate question and it is asked in open_questions.

engine.declared: goldfish_targets.json declares seven targets: a ten-card symmetric table-draw engine, a six-card asymmetric punisher group, their conjunction, a commander-gated tax engine, an eight-card counterspell shell, win-condition access — and THE KILL, which rests on one card.

components.reading: The gift. Ten copies, 53.7% of openers, 85.2% ever and 75.4% by turn six, mean turn 2.507. The fattest component and the one that arrives first — which is the problem, because on its own it is a donation to three seats.

The bill. Six copies, 36.4% of openers, 67.2% ever and 55.9% by turn six, mean turn 3.045. deck-audit does not flag it — its `thin` test is size <= 3 and its single-point filter is size <= 1, so a six-card group sits outside both by design. The judgment that six is too few for the component that makes the gift asymmetric is mine, not the audit's. Win-condition access is thinner still at five, but it holds two tutors; this group holds none, so a seventh copy here is the step the corpus prices at 36.4% → 41%.

The conjunction the deck actually wins with: 56.7% ever, 41.2% by turn six, mean turn 4.215. Both halves arrive within a turn and a half of each other on average; the gap between 85.2% and 56.7% is entirely the punisher's.
The commander-gated tax and doubling layer: 41.2% of openers, 63.8% ever, 44.4% by turn six, mean turn 5.488. This is the target that is gated on Heliod actually being cast, and Heliod is {2}{W}{W}.

Eight free-or-cheap answers, 45.6% of openers, 78.1% ever, 67.2% by turn six, mean turn 2.764. This is the deck's real protection budget and it is healthy; do not buy a fifth dedicated protection card on the strength of the protection axis reading 1.

Win-condition ACCESS: 31.2% of openers, 61.2% ever, 50.5% by turn six. Read the group before the number — two of the five are tutors and the group never names Hullbreaker Horror, without which Aetherflux Reservoir is a life-gain artifact rather than a kill.

THE KILL, and its thinnest component is one card. 7.1% of opening sevens, 9.1% by turn three; the whole four-card target assembles in 0.7% of games (2.4% with the modelled tutor), 0.3% by turn six, mean turn 6.809. This is the deck's ceiling, not its plan, and the strategic frame already says so.

lean_into.what: Sequence the punisher before the engine, and mulligan on that axis.
lean_into.why: The deck's asymmetry runs backwards. Duke's rule is that enablers at least dig toward payoffs — but this deck's enablers dig for all four seats, one card to you and three to the table per cycle. A turn-two Ebony Owl Netsuke does nothing and costs nothing; a turn-two Howling Mine with no punisher is a gift to whoever is fastest. The gift arrives at mean turn 2.507 and the bill at 3.045, so the default sequencing is exactly wrong. The pod run says who collects: heliod was eliminated in 14 of 20 games, 8 by the aggro seat on damage and 5 by the drain seat on life loss.

add_candidates.closes: engine component: the six-card punisher group (measured 0.672 ever, 0.559 by turn six)
add_candidates.why: 'At the beginning of the chosen player's upkeep, this artifact deals X damage to that player, where X is the number of cards in their hand minus 4' — Iron Maiden's clause for {1} instead of {3}, aimed at one opponent instead of all three. It is a seventh copy of the component this document argues is the thin one, and the corpus prices that step: seven copies is 41% of openers against six copies' 36.4%. Say the weakness out loud — it charges one seat where Iron Maiden charges all three, so it is a worse card bought two mana cheaper, and its slot only makes sense as the swap out of the card that pays the whole table.

open_questions.question: Re-run mana-analysis and goldfish on the list with the basics at 11 Islands / 6 Plains and the four mana adds applied (Sea of Clouds, Floodfarm Verge, Mystic Gate, Chromatic Lantern), and report colour-sources, on_curve_probability and the turn-three land-drop rate against the current -18 / W 0.515 / 0.866.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every figure I give for the package is recomputed by me through manabase's functions on a hypothetical 99, not read from a tracked artifact. They are the size of the prescription and should be measured before four slots are spent. The land-drop rate in particular can only fall or hold: Chromatic Lantern is a spell where Metallurgic Summonings was, and Mystic Gate replaces a land one for one.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json's 'Win condition access' group names Approach of the Second Sun, Aetherflux Reservoir, Mystical Tutor, Jace Wielder of Mysteries and Enlightened Tutor, and never names Hullbreaker Horror — without which the Reservoir is not a kill. Should that group be split into 'Approach access' and 'Reservoir access', and both measured?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 61.2% ever and 50.5% by turn six is the deck's most-quoted number and it measures a group containing two tutors and not containing the creature the kill runs on. The separate THE KILL target measures 0.7%. A reader comparing 50.5% with 0.7% is comparing two different claims about the same plan.

open_questions.question: Re-run goldfish with Black Vise added to the punisher any_of group and Forced Fruition removed from the table-draw group, and report the new 'Engine + punisher assembled' by-turn-six rate against the current 41.2%.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two changes push the conjunction in opposite directions — the payoff group gains a seventh member while the gift group loses its tenth — and the sign of the net is the whole case for the swap. Black Vise is ranked last for that reason.

open_questions.question: With Forced Fruition cut, does the punisher clock still resolve as stack 003 proved it does? Build the equivalent board — Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke with Howling Mine or Font of Mythos as the gift — and resolve an opponent's upkeep under a Naturalize on the gift.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 003 is the deck's proof that the median plan works and Forced Fruition is the enchantment on its board. Cutting it does not break the clock in Magic terms, but it does leave the clock without a checker-passed artifact, and this document may not assert the replacement works.

open_questions.question: Teferi's Protection cast on the turn BEFORE yours: 'Until your next turn, your life total can't change', and the phased-out permanents phase in before your untap step. Do the restriction and the phase-out both end before your first main phase, so it can be held on an opponent's end step and the Aetherflux Reservoir ledger still run on your own turn?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Whether the one protection card the audit counts is usable the turn before the kill decides whether the shield and the kill can share a game at all — and the turn before you commit is when the table's interaction actually shows up.

open_questions.question: Does Grand Abolisher's static close every priority window stack 006 leaves open, including a channel ability activated from a card in hand (Otawara, Soaring City)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame carries Grand Abolisher as the protection plan for the deck's own kill and simultaneously flags it unverified. The kill is checker-passed; the shield around it is not. Grand Abolisher is also {W}{W}, so this question and the colour-sources finding are the same question asked twice.

open_questions.question: Is there a strategy section to be written on forced-draw / group-hug punisher archetypes — specifically, the arithmetic of when a symmetric draw effect pays for itself against three opponents?
open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame lists this as its own first gap. Every judgment here about gift-versus-payoff timing leans on multiplayer.asymmetry and mulligans.engine-hands, neither of which was written about a deck whose enablers help the table.

gaps: This diagnosis was re-run because manabase.land_colors and mana_analysis.nonland_producer_kind were reading PARENTHESISED REMINDER TEXT as a card's own ability — 24 cards in the corpus, every one a Treasure-maker. In this deck the two affected cards are Smothering Tithe and An Offer You Can't Refuse, and the second is the sharper illustration: its Treasures go to the countered spell's controller, so an opponent's mana was being counted as five of this deck's colour sources. The decklist has not changed (sha 2d7f07f9… still matches cards.json); only the measurement did. colour-sources moved from -16 to -18, W total sources from 20 to 18, U from 31 to 29, and W on-curve from 0.58 to 0.515. The previous verdict for the axis was already 'liability'; the direction was right and the size was understated.

The Karsten target of 36 is the repo's own hypergeometric at turn three on the play over 99 cards, not Karsten's published figure. His table gives 33 sources for {C}{C} (Grand Abolisher), 29 for 1{C}{C} (Supreme Verdict) and 26 for 2{C}{C} (the commander). 18 is under all three, so the finding does not depend on which number you prefer — but a reader who wants the smallest honest gap should use 26 and read it as short eight for the commander, not short eighteen.

W's effective_pips is 2 by exactly the quorum and no margin: PIP_WEIGHT_QUORUM is 0.20, 15 cards carry a white pip, ceil(15 × 0.20) = 3, and exactly three cards want {W}{W}. Cut Grand Abolisher or Supreme Verdict and white's effective requirement falls to one pip and its target falls with it. That is a real sensitivity in the measure and the pilot should know it before spending four slots — but the commander is one of the three and cannot be cut, so the requirement cannot be legislated below {W}{W}.

Every figure for the proposed mana package is RECOMPUTED by me through manabase's own functions on a hypothetical 99, not read from a tracked artifact. It is ◆ by construction and reproducible — the harness reproduces mana_analysis.json exactly on the base list — but it is not mana_analysis.json. The first open question exists to replace it with a measurement.

Two candidates were considered and REJECTED on how the measure reads them, and both rejections are about the tool rather than the card. Port Town would be a fine untapped WU dual, but enters_tapped_unconditionally reads it as an unconditional tapland — its escape clause says 'you may reveal', not 'unless' and not 'you may pay' — so it would move the taplands axis 2 → 3 for a benefit Floodfarm Verge delivers without it. Hengegate Pathway // Mistgate Pathway is credited by land_colors with BOTH W and U because the function reads the combined faces, which is wrong for a modal DFC where you choose one face on the way in; its true contribution is one source of whichever colour you picked.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256 (deck-audit's freshness block reports it null), so every bracket_delta here was recomputed directly through bracket.assess rather than read from it. Base floor 4, and all six paired swaps land on 4.

No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness reports recon.present false) and `deck-notes heliod list` reports no log entries and no log_annotations.json. Nothing here is weighed against what strong Heliod, the Radiant Dawn lists actually run, or against anything that happened at a real table. The Forced Fruition and Mikokoro cuts in particular are argued from this deck's artifacts and the corpus alone.

The table evidence is ONE run of 20 games — giada-angels-vs-vito-vs-baylen-tokens-n20-92280ee6-s452098790, seeded — with Forge's AI on every seat including ours. Its own assumptions block quotes Forge as 'best with aggro and midrange decks, poor to ok in control decks', so heliod's 0.1 win rate (ci95 [0.028, 0.301]) is a lower bound and not a measurement of the deck. That is why the conversion finding rests on the ZERO attributed eliminations and the flat damage curve — shapes the AI caveat does not erase — rather than on the win rate. A second run against a different pod would say whether the aggro seat is the deck's problem or that pod's.

card_roles.json classifies 85.9% of this deck and the twelve unclassified cards are not incidental — Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke and Propaganda are the deck's identity. Every role-derived axis count above is a floor, and I have said so where it changes the reading.

The sweepers axis carries a target of 5-7 from the control archetype override while quoting a source that says one or two max. The corpus cannot settle which applies to a deck that never needs the board clear; I called it adequate on the quote rather than the override, and a reader may reasonably disagree.
